result.title: Decoupling Perception from Generation for Agentic 3D CT Report Generation
result.summary: Chest CT reports repeatedly assess the same anatomical regions for findings and their attributes, such as whether a lung nodule is present and where it is located. These assessments suggest learning to answer visual questions directly, rather than coupling perception to open-ended text generation. Yet current CT report generation models largely follow generic vision-language modeling, which may miss subtle abnormalities when training data are limited. We therefore formulate report generation as a set of visual question-answering decisions coordinated by a large language model (LLM) agent. This decouples visual perception from reasoning and report writing: perception can be learned as a discriminative, non-generative task, while the LLM focuses on reasoning over patient context and posing relevant visual queries. We introduce Rad-VL-JEPA, which unifies report retrieval, finding recognition, and fine-grained attribute characterization through vision-language joint-embedding prediction. Building on this perception module, an agent trained with reinforcement learning (RL) acquires patient-specific visual evidence, while a separate editor incorporates the evidence into the final report, further separating evidence acquisition from report realization. Experiments show that Rad-VL-JEPA achieves strong performance on fine-grained CT understanding tasks with lower amortized per-query inference time than a generative VLM baseline trained with the same CT encoder and VQA data. The resulting reporting system outperforms strong VLM-based and agentic baselines.

AI.brief_summary: 该文把 3D 胸部 CT 报告生成重构为 LLM agent 协调的一组视觉问答决策：用 JEPA 式视觉-语言联合嵌入预测训练判别式（非生成）感知模块，完成报告检索、病灶识别与细粒度属性刻画，再由 RL 训练的 agent 主动获取患者视觉证据，并交由独立编辑器成文。
AI.relevance_reason: 与「视觉证据筛选」及把感知与推理/生成解耦的关注直接相关；可供核查 agent 的查询与证据取舍是否真正决定最终结论（而非装饰性调用）、判别式感知的 amortized 成本是否成立，以及证据以何种形式进入 LLM 推理。
